name: External covariate datasets for Ukrainian air-raid alert forecasting: (1) Kaggle 'Massive Missile Attacks on Ukraine' (piterfm), (2) VIINA 2.0 (Violent Incident Information from News Articles, zhukovyuri), (3) DiXi Group Energy Map 'massive strikes on critical infrastructure' dataset, (4) mdniprovskyi/time-machine-data (derived pipeline joining VIINA + Kaggle + alert seconds)
type: dataset (1-3: primary/secondary datasets; 4: derived student/hobby data repo of pre-aggregated JSON)
url: Kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/piterfm/massive-missile-attacks-on-ukraine (overview notebook https://www.kaggle.com/code/piterfm/massive-missile-attacks-on-ukraine-data-review) ; VIINA: https://github.com/zhukovyuri/VIINA (paper doi:10.1016/j.jce.2023.06.003) ; DiXi Energy Map dataset: https://map.ua-energy.org/en/datasets/9091d6f9-564f-434a-a9d2-bba9657ca2c1 (now 301-redirects to energy-map.info; page is JS-rendered) ; time-machine-data: https://github.com/mdniprovskyi/time-machine-data
year: [uncertain] Kaggle: version 215, last updated 2026-10-17 (near-daily updates since 2022/2023). VIINA 2.0: repo created 2022-03-07, last push 2026-10-14, updated daily. DiXi Energy Map strike dataset: listed period 11.09.2022-17.11.2024, update date 18.11.2024, 'not regularly' [uncertain whether a newer version exists in 2026]. time-machine-data: created 2026-08-18, last push 2026-09-16; covers VIINA to 2026-08-20, Kaggle to 2026-08-14, alert seconds to 2026-08-29. All checked 2026-10-17.
authors: [uncertain] Kaggle: Petro Ivaniuk (piterfm), manual curation from Ukrainian Air Force Command and General Staff posts (Facebook/Telegram), occasional corrections from Monitor/Monitorwar Telegram channels. VIINA: Yuri M. Zhukov (Georgetown) and Natalie Ayers. Energy Map: DiXi Group think tank (site formerly USAID-supported), compiled from official Armed Forces reports. time-machine-data: GitHub user mdniprovskyi [uncertain real identity].
popularity: Kaggle: 138 votes, 22,592 downloads, 49,225 views, 18 notebooks, usability 1.0; cited by BBC, USA Today, CSIS, War Quants. VIINA: 360 GitHub stars, JCE 2023 paper. Energy Map: portal claims 420+ datasets; strike dataset widely quoted by Interfax-Ukraine in DiXi reports. time-machine-data: 0 stars.
peer_review_status: Kaggle: self-curated dataset, not peer-reviewed (but transcribes official military reports). VIINA: peer-reviewed methodology paper (Zhukov 2023, Journal of Comparative Economics); data itself is ML-classified news, self-reported accuracy tables in README. DiXi Energy Map: NGO/think-tank compilation, not peer-reviewed. time-machine-data: unreviewed derived repo, no README, no license.
target_type: Not applicable: these are covariate sources, not forecasting studies. Relevant to our ONSET target only as candidate exogenous features (attack intensity, front activity) and as explanation of regime shifts in onset rate. Note time-machine-data's 'time-under-alert' metric is a STATE aggregate (seconds under alert per city-day), not onsets.
target_definition: Not applicable. Kaggle unit = one attack record (time_start, time_end, model, launch_place, target, launched, destroyed, not_reach_goal, still_attacking, affected_region, ...). VIINA unit = one geocoded news report (date, time HH:MM of report, ADM1_NAME oblast, lat/lon, GEO_PRECISION, source, url, text) with BERT labels (t_airstrike, t_uav, t_aad, t_airalert, t_artillery, ...; actor a_rus_init, ...). Energy Map = daily counts of missiles/drones fired and shot down during massive strikes. time-machine-data = city x calendar-date (Europe/Kyiv) records: airAttackRecorded, viinaEventCount, nightRaid (00:00-07:00), missiles, attackDrones, civilianDeaths, airAlertSeconds, explosionReports.
spatial_unit: Kaggle: national per attack, with free-text target/affected_region (city, oblast, 'direction' or all Ukraine) - not a clean oblast panel. VIINA: populated place / point with ADM1 (oblast) name+code; control data at GeoNames (33,141) or KATOTTH (29,724) places. Energy Map: national daily. time-machine-data: 23 canonical cities (oblast capitals; exact-city geocode only).
at_risk_masking: Not applicable (no forecasting target). For our use: any join must happen on the hourly oblast grid AFTER our at-risk mask; covariates do not change which rows are masked.
data_sources: Kaggle: official UA Air Force Command and General Staff daily reports since Oct 2022 (massive strikes) plus some single shot-down UAVs; companion table missiles_and_uavs.csv (category, origin, guidance, unit cost). VIINA: 16 UA/RU outlets (24tv, Espreso, Forbes UA, Interfax-UA, KP, Liga, Liveuamap, Militarnyi, Mediazona, Meduza, NV, NG, NTV, Ukrainska Pravda, RIA, UNIAN), scraped every 6 h, geocoded via Yandex/OSM; control layers from DeepStateMap, ISW, Wikipedia; yearly files 2022-2026. Energy Map: official Armed Forces reports, 2022-09-11 to 2024-11-17 (listed). time-machine-data: VIINA + Kaggle + OHCHR casualty floors + air-alarms.in.ua explosion reports + an alert-seconds file + GeoConfirmed geojson; 2022-02-24 to 2026-08-31.
data_source_variant: [uncertain] None of these are alert sources, so official/volunteer/API variant is not directly applicable. Exception: time-machine-data's airAlertSeconds comes from an unnamed 'daily_alert_seconds_corrected.csv' with oblast/raion/hromada alerts 'unioned upstream' at city level, ending 2026-08-29 (consistent with the official-file gap) [uncertain which alert source it is]. Kaggle snapshot is versioned on Kaggle (v215 on 2026-10-17); VIINA keeps only 'latest' files, older vintages by email request.
preprocessing: Kaggle: if only destroyed is published, launched := destroyed as a lower bound (status_data flags it; 'hidden' = not published); null = unknown. VIINA: 'one-per-day' filter (event_1pd) merges same actor+tactic reports in the same place on the same day; manual inspection of geocodes. time-machine-data: VIINA attack rule = Russian initiator AND (airstrike OR UAV), exact-city geocode, max casualty count per location/date, weapons attributed only when a single city/oblast is confirmed; null vs 0 explicitly distinguished; no extrapolation.
known_label_artefacts: [uncertain] Kaggle: (a) the Ukrainian Air Force stopped reporting counts for some missile types from 2026-08-10 (dataset banner) - a reporting-regime break INSIDE our final test window (2026-07-27 to 09-07); (b) launched imputed from destroyed (lower bound); (c) 'not_reach_goal' only from Jul 2024, 'border_crossing'/'still_attacking' added later - columns appear mid-series; (d) target field mixes cities, oblasts, directions, 'all Ukraine'; (e) records often aggregated per overnight wave, so hourly placement is coarse. VIINA: (a) date/time is report publication time, not event time; (b) ML labels with moderate precision (README tables, e.g. t_airalert ~0.81 precision/0.72 recall in one table) [uncertain exact metric definitions]; (c) source set changes over time; (d) 'latest' files may be re-processed so values are not vintage-stable [uncertain]; (e) contains t_airalert label = news about alerts, i.e. a noisy copy of our target. Energy Map: massive strikes only, irregular updates, stale since Nov 2024 [uncertain]. time-machine-data: explosionReports are media report counts, not physical explosions; deletes/re-uploads files (no versioning discipline); no license.
model_family: Not applicable (datasets). Downstream use would be extra columns in our GBM/LR onset model, or a regime-shift explanatory analysis (descriptive regression of weekly onset rate on weekly launched drones).
features: Candidate features, all lagged so known at t: (1) Kaggle: launched/destroyed drones and missiles in the last 24h/7d nationally (by category Shahed-type UAV vs cruise vs ballistic), attacks completed before t; rolling 30-day drone launch rate as a regime indicator. (2) VIINA: count of t_airstrike/t_uav/t_artillery reports per oblast in the last 24h/7d with report time < t; frontline proximity / share of oblast places CONTESTED or RU from control data (slow, daily). (3) Energy Map: count of massive strikes in last 30d (only to 2024). (4) time-machine-data: daily city-level attack flags - only usable as day-lagged features for 23 cities. Avoid VIINA t_airalert (target proxy).
external_feature_timing: [uncertain] Critical. Kaggle: an overnight attack is published by the Air Force typically the next morning (Kyiv) after it ends [uncertain exact lag, often ~08:00-10:00 Kyiv], and the dataset adds it with a further manual lag (versions near-daily); time_start/time_end are event times, so using them as-of time_start is ORACLE leakage - availability time must be max(time_end, publication) + curation lag; also counts get revised. VIINA: has minute-precision report time (publication), but the scraper runs every 6 h and the release is daily, so real-time availability is <= 6-24 h after publication; news reports themselves often follow the alert/strike, so same-hour VIINA features are effectively observing the outcome. Energy Map: irregular update, unusable live. time-machine-data: calendar-day aggregates in Europe/Kyiv, so any value for day D is known only after D ends (use with >= 1 day lag); daily-local aggregation conflicts with our UTC hourly grid. For backtests, without archived vintages one can only approximate availability with a conservative fixed lag (e.g. 24 h).
ablation_design: Not applicable (no study). For our project: any covariate ablation must use the same time-restricted sample - Kaggle starts Oct 2022, Energy Map ends Nov 2024, time-machine-data ends Aug 2026, VIINA control files are yearly - so compare model with vs without covariates on the intersection period only, with identical train/val/test cut-offs.
split_scheme: Not applicable. Coverage vs our splits: Kaggle covers train (from 2022-10) and the full test window, but with the 2026-08-10 reporting break; VIINA covers everything; Energy Map does not cover validation or test; time-machine-data stops 2026-08-14/20/29 depending on metric, i.e. mid-test - not usable for the frozen test.
baseline_strength: Not applicable. Relevant point: the rolling recent-rate baseline (D-021) already absorbs slow regime shifts like the Jan-2025 drone surge that Kaggle launch counts would explain, so external intensity features are unlikely to beat it unless they lead the alert process by hours.
calibration_under_drift: Useful for EXPLAINING drift, not for calibration: Kaggle monthly launched-UAV totals document the large rise in drone volume in 2025-2026 (BBC: attacks doubled after Jan 2025), which is a plausible cause of base-rate shifts between train and test and of the yellow (drone) dominance after the Sep-2026 reform. Stated as hypothesis per D-015.
regime_coverage: Kaggle spans the Jan-2025 drone surge and the 2026-08-10 reporting change, and is current to 2026-10-17, so it overlaps the new yellow/red regime (2026-09-13 onward) - the only covariate that could descriptively compare drone volume before vs after the reform. VIINA spans all regimes. Energy Map covers 2022-2024 only. time-machine-data ends before the reform.
leakage_handling: Main leakage risks if adopted: (1) event-time vs availability-time: Kaggle time_start/time_end and VIINA report time must be shifted to when the record was observable; (2) retroactive revision: Kaggle versions and VIINA 'latest' files are rewritten, so backtests use future-corrected values - the leakage truncation test (tests/test_leakage.py) cannot catch this because the file itself is post-hoc; (3) VIINA t_airalert and same-hour UAV news are near-copies of the label; (4) daily aggregates (time-machine-data, Kaggle per-day) read across the whole calendar day including hours after t; (5) whole-file statistics (e.g. normalising launch counts by series max) fit on test. Mitigation: fixed conservative lag (>= 24 h for daily data), features computed only from records with availability_time <= t, add each covariate to the truncation test.
test_window_hygiene: Not applicable. For our project the covariates would have to be chosen before seeing final-test numbers; adding them post-M4 would be a new milestone requiring Oleksandr's approval and a new dependency/data source decision.
headline_results: No forecasting results (datasets). Descriptive facts: Kaggle v215 (2026-10-17), 916 KB, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0, two tables; reporting of some missile types stopped 2026-08-10. VIINA 2.0: daily updates, ODbL, minute-precision report time, oblast ADM1 codes. DiXi: 25 massive missile-drone attacks on energy Sep 2022-Sep 2024 (>1,400 missiles, ~500 UAVs); early-2026 report: >= 64 massive energy attacks since Feb 2022 with ~12,700 UAVs and ~2,900 missiles (headline elsewhere says 12,900 UAVs - inconsistent). time-machine-data: 2026 records 913 city-days (to 2026-08-20) of attack flags; mostly null missile/drone attributions.
code_available: [uncertain] Kaggle: data downloadable with Kaggle account/API, CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (non-commercial, share-alike), actively maintained. VIINA: GitHub zip CSVs + geojson, ODbL, actively maintained. Energy Map: web portal with API description, terms of service, no explicit dataset license found, JS-rendered pages [uncertain license]. time-machine-data: JSON + 17.5 MB GeoConfirmed geojson on GitHub, no license, no README, no code (pipeline not published).
takeaways_for_project: 1) Do NOT add any of these to the frozen M4 model: CLAUDE.md forbids new data/dependencies without Oleksandr's approval, and the features must be computable from data with timestamp <= t, which none of them guarantees without vintages. Log as FUTURE WORK. 2) Best use is explanatory (D-015 hypotheses): plot Kaggle weekly launched UAVs vs our national weekly onset rate to explain the Jan-2025 surge and the post-reform yellow-dominated regime; state as hypothesis, not cause. 3) Kaggle's 2026-08-10 reporting break falls inside our final test window: any feature from it would shift distribution mid-test. 4) If ever used as features: shift to availability time with a conservative >= 24 h lag, aggregate in UTC (not Kyiv-day), map oblast names only via src/regions.py (no fuzzy matching, D-017), and extend tests/test_leakage.py with a negative control that uses un-lagged event times. 5) Never use VIINA t_airalert (label proxy). 6) Energy Map and time-machine-data do not cover the test window - discard for modelling. 7) Mixing sources: keep covariates out of the new-regime exploratory scoring unless the same lag rule applies in both periods.
best_practices: Adopt: explicit availability timestamps per external record; null-vs-zero distinction (as time-machine-data does); conservative fixed lags when no vintage archive exists; ablation on the common coverage period; snapshot/version pinning (Kaggle version number, VIINA download date) recorded in run_meta.json. Avoid: joining by event time (oracle); daily-local aggregates on an hourly UTC grid; treating imputed lower bounds (Kaggle launched := destroyed) as true counts; using news-derived alert labels; relying on unlicensed/unversioned derived repos (time-machine-data) instead of primary sources; claiming causal explanation of regime shifts from correlated intensity series.
